The repro already triggers E0567/E0568 on the malformed `auto trait` items, so the AST validation layer is the upstream gate that recognizes the invalid syntax. If recovery after those errors leaves broken items in the pipeline, this is the first place to inspect.

The crash is an orphan-check assertion on an auto trait with generic parameters, so the crate’s generic-collection step is a plausible source of the bad parameter accounting that later coherence code sees. This file builds `ty::Generics` for items and is where malformed generics can be propagated downstream.

Orphan checking and coherence overlap ultimately rely on trait-selection coherence logic, and this file owns the overlap/unification machinery used to judge impl coherence. It is a strong candidate for the mismatch between the malformed auto-trait input and the assertion in coherence.

This module coordinates the broader checking phase that feeds coherence and related queries. If malformed auto-trait items are not short-circuited after earlier diagnostics, the orchestration here can still drive the later coherence path that panics.

As the HIR-analysis crate root, this wires together collection, coherence, checking, and other analyses. It is less specific than the coherence submodules, but it is still part of the control path that can let invalid items reach orphan checking.

Auto traits and other special traits use built-in coherence rules, and this module handles compiler-enforced trait-impl restrictions. It is relevant because the crash is specific to auto-trait handling rather than ordinary trait coherence.

The reproducer hits the auto-trait feature gate path as well as the syntactic validation path. This module is less likely than coherence, but it is part of the upstream acceptance/rejection of the malformed `auto trait` definitions.

The coherence and orphan checks depend on the trait solver’s selection engine to reason about impls and trait obligations. If the malformed auto-trait parameters distort selection inputs, this is a downstream but still plausible contributor.
